articles.summary: Transfer pricing is a critical concept for multinational businesses and international contractors. Essentially, transfer pricing concerns the prices charged for goods, services, or intellectual property (IP) between related entities within an enterprise, such as between a parent company and its subsidiaries. While this might appear simple, it can become complex when transactions span international borders and involve various tax jurisdictions. This is where the arm's length principle comes into play—a cornerstone of transfer pricing rules used by numerous countries and integral to understanding international taxation.
articles.title: What is the arm's length principle in transfer pricing for international contractors?
